rounds.learn: A function is a named recipe. def makes one. The code inside only runs when you call the function by its name with ().
rounds.task: Make a greet function. Call it twice.
rounds.say: hello, twice. One recipe, used two times.

rounds.learn: A function can take inputs, called parameters. return hands an answer back to whoever called it.

rounds.task: Write add, which takes a and b and returns their sum. Print add(2, 3).
rounds.say: 5. You wrote a function and used it.

rounds.task: Write a function called square that returns a number times itself. Print square(9).
rounds.hint: def square(n): and under it return n * n. Then print(square(9)).

checks.msg: Hand the answer back with return.

rounds.say: 81. Your own recipe, written from nothing.
